Subject: FintechAI — pricing & latency tradeoffs (post-call recap)

Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of needs (from call):
- Primary use case: real-time risk scoring + short conversational agent for customer support.
- Expected monthly token volume: ~12M–18M tokens (pilot → scale).
- Typical request size: 700–1,200 tokens (prompt + response); modal ~900 tokens.
- Peak concurrency: 35–50 concurrent requests during peak hours.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target ~250–350ms for single-turn scoring requests; conversational flows can tolerate 600–800ms.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC peering later in expansion.

Primary questions / asks for pricing qualification:
1) Can you confirm a budget range for inference (monthly)? Even a ballpark helps us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated.
2) Target unit economics: is there a target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for?
3) Any hard latency ceilings (e.g., max p95 = 300ms) that would force Dedicated?

Latency vs cost tradeoffs (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest path, no ops, streaming responses reduce perceived latency for long outputs, batch/quantization choices can lower cost but may increase tail latency.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale, and easier to hit tighter p95 through reserved GPU pools and reduced multi-tenancy jitter.
- Config knobs we discussed: batching window, streaming enabled/disabled, KV cache prefixing, and quantization profile (int8 vs fp16) — all affect unit cost and latency.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm budget range + target $/1M tokens and any strict p95 requirement.
- Us: produce a tailored cost estimate (hosted vs dedicated), include expected $/1M tokens, and recommended config options (batch sizes, streaming, tier).
- Optionally: we can spin up a short perf trial on hosted to validate p95 under your payload.

Attachments: I attached a quick pricing worksheet to illustrate tradeoffs (redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx).

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick clarifications / numbers from our side:

1) Budget: pilot phase ~ $3k–5k / month; post-pilot (if results look good) we plan for a launch budget in the $30k–$50k / month range (we'd want a path to ~1–2 year committed pricing if ROI looks solid).
2) Target $/1M tokens: we'd like to get to roughly $75–85 per 1M tokens at scale (this is our internal target to make the unit economics work for our pricing model).
3) Latency: for scoring endpoints we need p95 < 350ms. For the conversational agent, 600ms p95 is acceptable.
4) Volume confirmation: aiming for 12M tokens/month in pilot, scaling to ~120M tokens/month over 9–12 months if adoption is good.
5) Peak concurrency: can reach up to 50 concurrent scoring requests; typical during peak: 40.

Happy to move forward with a hosted trial to validate latency, but if hitting p95 < 350ms consistently will require dedicated tiers we should get that in the cost proposal.

Appreciate the attachment — we reviewed it briefly and have a few questions about the assumptions for batch sizes and streaming. Can you call out the changes that drive down to ~$80/1M?

Alex — thanks, this is super helpful. Short answers and what I'll include in the proposal:

Why we can get to ~$80/1M tokens (assumptions & levers):
- Dedicated reserved pools: committed capacity discounts reduce base $/token at higher volumes. For your target 100–120M tokens, dedicated reserved pricing can drop unit cost by ~30–40% vs on-demand hosted.
- Quantization & smaller model variants for scoring: using an int8-quantized scoring model where quality is preserved for short inputs reduces per-token GPU time.
- Batching for scoring endpoints: because scoring requests are short (model steps limited), we can use continuous batching (small windows, e.g., 10–20ms) to increase utilization with minimal tail impact.
- Streaming: for longer conversational outputs, streaming reduces perceived latency but doesn't reduce token cost; it does reduce time-to-first-byte which helps UX.

Tradeoffs to call out in the proposal:
- If you need strict p95 < 300ms 100% of the time (even at 50 concurrency), that likely pushes us to a Dedicated tier with higher reserve and narrower batch windows — costs go up.
- If you accept p95 ~350ms for scoring and 600ms for conv flows, a Hosted+optimizations mix can hit ~$80/1M at mid-scale with a favorable reserved commit.

Next steps (I'll take these):
- Draft two-line pricing options: Hosted (with recommended batch/stream settings) and Dedicated (1-year commit) with expected $/1M tokens at 12M, 50M, and 120M monthly volumes.
- Include a config appendix that lists batch window, streaming on/off, quantization profile, and expected p95 ranges per config.
- Add a recommended pilot (2 weeks on hosted with our perf harness) to validate p95 at your payload.

I attached a sanitized CSV with example numbers (fintechai-pricing-sheet.csv) and will follow with a formal proposal/DocuSign link once you confirm which scenarios you want priced.

If you're good, I'll aim to send the formal proposal by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
